author: barnabasbusa
content:
I don't wanna sound harsh or split hairs, but 7251 was proposed in 2023, got included in Electra on 21 March 2024 (ACDC 130), spec was pretty much done by December 2024 and it went live in May 2025. So if you launched early 2025, 0x02 had already been in scope for about a year.
Also we said back then already that the validator count is a problem. with PQ it's a much bigger one.

PQ registration is a request from the withdrawal address, same as switching to compounding. so if your contract can't do one it can't do the other, and you have to touch it for PQ anyway. what's the extra cost of 0x02 on top of that?

why would you have to centralize under a single operator? 0x02 doesn't force you to consolidate, your operators can keep running 32 ETH validators

author: yorickdowne
content: If they run on a single operator, they don't need the reward distribution contract. That's why they'd just centralize, instead of upgrading contract.

author: wander1
content:
Not splitting hairs at all! This touches directly on our logic for using 0x01. Although we were certainly aware of 0x02 discussions when we began planning and building, we can only build on what exists, and features are discussed and proposed and moved between hard forks all the time. I mentioned May 2025 because that's when the EIP was moved to Final (about a week after Pectra happened), and it says nothing about deprecating 0x01. My understanding of the discussion at the time was that 0x02 would be launched and everyone would monitor adoption to see if further steps were needed to reduce validator count. At the time, total ETH staked had not grown for ~9 months, and we couldn't wait for 0x02 to design and build and launch because waiting has its own costs.

In the end, we made a calculated bet that 0x01 would not be deprecated before we recouped our investment. We felt this was justified because of the above but also based on the continuation of 0x00 validators after 0x01 was added. If this deprecation does happen, we will have been wrong. The lesson we would learn in that case is that Ethereum's staking interface is less stable than anticipated, and therefore our decentralized system is too costly to maintain. Yorick is right, and it's a simple numbers thing: the cost to centralize our staking operations is about the same as updating to 0x02, but future maintenance will be vastly cheaper. We wanted this distributed staking system to provide long-term value, but Ethereum may be evolving too fast for a relatively small staking org to do this kind of decentralization right now. Sounds like it would be tough for Rocket Pool as well. Of course, I'm sure Lido will do just fine.

If we centralize, we would of course migrate entirely to 0x02 validators. I think the core question is whether 0x02 and reducing validator count is more important for Ethereum right now than fighting staking centralization. Or at least that's what the conflict looks like from where I'm sitting. I've mentioned my own preference on that and already gave my suggestion re: 0x02 incentives above, so at this point I'll just monitor the discussion to see what happens. I know we're not a big force in this space, but hopefully my perspective is helpful.
